plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether a quarter-wave Bragg reflector stack, tuned to the UV band center (300 nm), can simultaneously achieve high UV reflection and high SWIR transmission using HfO2/SiO2 on fused silica. The prior knowledge is that quarter-wave stacks produce high reflectance at their design wavelength and its odd harmonics, while remaining relatively transparent at wavelengths far from the Bragg condition. This route was planned from the model's own prior knowledge alone, with no literature retrieval. The thickness initialization bounds are being tightened to 30-50 nm for HfO2 and 40-60 nm for SiO2 to seed candidates near the quarter-wave condition at 300 nm, correcting the previous iteration's detuned thicknesses (90-120 nm range).

routes.title: UV Bragg Reflector with SWIR Transmission Window using HfO2/SiO2 Quarter-Wave Stack
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 20-layer quarter-wave stack centered at 300 nm will produce high reflectance in the 200-400 nm UV band while maintaining high transmittance in the 800-1500 nm SWIR band, because the Bragg condition is satisfied at UV wavelengths but not at SWIR wavelengths.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave dielectric stacks produce constructive interference for reflection at the design wavelength when layer optical thicknesses equal λ/4. At wavelengths significantly longer than the design wavelength, the stack behaves more like a homogeneous medium with reduced reflectance. HfO2 provides high index contrast against SiO2, enabling strong UV reflection with fewer layers.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate (20 dielectric layers total, alternating HfO2 and SiO2 starting with HfO2)
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 20 layers, with HfO2 layers bounded to 30-50 nm and SiO2 layers bounded to 40-60 nm to seed near quarter-wave condition at 300 nm
soft_objectives: Maximize average reflectance in 200-400 nm band
Maximize average transmittance in 800-1500 nm band
Minimize total layer count while meeting performance targets
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness bounds reflect typical sputtering/evaporation precision for UV optical coatings
HfO2 and SiO2 are standard coating materials with known deposition processes
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stacks produce peak reflectance at the design wavelength where each layer has optical thickness λ/4
Reflectance bandwidth scales with index contrast: higher n_H/n_L ratio gives wider high-reflectance band
At wavelengths much longer than the quarter-wave design wavelength, the stack transmits more because phase conditions no longer support constructive reflection
HfO2 has refractive index approximately 2.0-2.1 in UV, SiO2 approximately 1.5, giving useful index contrast for UV mirrors
Fused silica substrate is transparent in both UV and SWIR bands, not limiting the design
expected_advantages: Quarter-wave seeding should converge faster than unbounded optimization
20 layers provides sufficient reflectance in UV while leaving margin under 30-layer limit
Alternating high/low index structure is a well-known reflector topology
Thickness bounds prevent optimizer from exploring physically unrealistic or manufacturing-difficult thicknesses
known_risks: I am recalling approximate refractive indices for HfO2 and SiO2 in UV; actual values from the material catalog may differ and affect quarter-wave thickness calculations
The quarter-wave condition at 300 nm may not optimally cover the full 200-400 nm band; band edges may have lower reflectance
I am uncertain whether 20 layers is optimal versus 18 or 22; this route fixes 20 and does not explore layer count as a variable
Dispersion of HfO2 and SiO2 across 200-1500 nm may shift the effective quarter-wave condition; I am not modeling dispersion explicitly in this hypothesis
The previous iteration achieved target_score ~0.56; I do not know if this thickness re-seeding will improve that without running the solver
What would settle these uncertainties: measured n/k dispersion data from the material catalog for hfo2 and sio2 across 200-1500 nm, and a layer-count sweep to find optimal pair number
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer planar dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Materials: alternating hfo2 and SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) layers, starting with hfo2 as layer 1. Total 20 dielectric layers (10 HfO2, 10 SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos)). Wavelength bands: 200-400 nm (maximize reflectance), 800-1500 nm (maximize transmittance). Design variables: individual thickness for each of the 20 layers. Thickness bounds: HfO2 layers 30-50 nm, SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) layers 40-60 nm. Incidence angle: 0 degrees (normal incidence). Polarization: unpolarized or both TE and TM averaged. Use gradient_thickness optimizer with increased mutation intensity for first two rounds to escape previous local optimum, then taper perturbation as scores improve.
routes.revision_reason: Continuation of control route with refined thickness initialization bounds per feedback directives: HfO2 30-50 nm, SiO2 40-60 nm, centered on quarter-wave condition at 300 nm to correct previous iteration's detuned thicknesses (90-120 nm range).

plan.knowledge_source_disclosure: This route was planned from the model's own prior knowledge alone. No Semantic Scholar query was issued, no retrieved paper reached the prompt, and no method-research report was supplied -- neither for the initial plan nor for any continuation round. It is the control arm of a controlled comparison against the literature-grounded routes, and its evidence-id allowlist is empty by construction.
unresolved_decisions: Whether 20 layers is the optimal count versus 18, 22, or other values within the 30-layer limit
Exact refractive index dispersion of hfo2 and sio2 from 200-1500 nm as stored in the material catalog
Whether normal incidence (0 degrees) is the correct assumption for UAV camera windows or if oblique incidence should be considered
The optimal quarter-wave center wavelength (300 nm chosen as band center, but 250 nm or 350 nm might better cover the 200-400 nm band)
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If all routes in this study fail to produce physically valid candidates with target_score above 0.5, the problem may require relaxing material constraints, increasing layer count limit, or accepting that simultaneous UV reflection and SWIR transmission with only HfO2/SiO2 is not achievable within 30 layers.

expected_observations: best_target_score should rise compared to iteration 03's 0.5606 if quarter-wave seeding improves convergence
valid_candidates count should remain similar or increase if thickness bounds are physically realizable
tightest_margin should not fall across rounds if the optimizer is finding robust solutions
thicknesses_nm should cluster around 39-40 nm for HfO2 and 50-52 nm for SiO2 if quarter-wave condition is being approached
run_status should remain 'completed' without optimization failures
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates falls below 5 for two consecutive rounds, reduce mutation intensity and continue for one more round before stopping
if thicknesses_nm converge to within 1 nm variation across all candidates for three consecutive rounds, stop and keep the current best

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.
